overview.description: Malilla is a point-trick game for four players in fixed partnerships, popular in Mexico and originating in Spain. Played with a 40-card Spanish deck, the Seven is the highest card (Malilla), ranking above Ace. Partners score card points (7=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one per trick; first team to 35 cumulative points wins. Trump is set by the dealer's last card turned face up.
overview.originName: Malilla (juego de cartas español y mexicano)

history.origins: Dates back to the 16th or 17th century. Its name is derived from the word for 'little bad one', referring to the powerful low-numbered cards.
timeline: 1600s: Mentioned in Spanish literature as a favorite among the nobility.
1800s: Spreads to the Spanish colonies in the Americas and the Philippines.
Present: Remains a traditional favorite in rural Spain and some Latin American regions.
20th Century: Largely superseded in popularity by games like Mus or Tute, but preserved in cultural heritage societies.
history.evolution: Spanish Malilla (Seven high) influenced the French game Manille (32-card, 10 high). Mexican Malilla keeps the 40-card Spanish pack with 7 as Malilla.
history.cultural: A game of social bonding, traditionally played in 'casinos' (private social clubs) in Spanish towns.

setup.deck: 40 cards: Suits are Oros (Coins), Copas (Cups), Espadas (Swords), Bastos (Clubs).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 10 cards. The dealer flips the last card to determine the Trump suit.

rules.objective: Your partnership must win tricks containing the high-value point cards (Seven=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one point per trick, and be the first team to reach 35 or more cumulative points to win the game.
rules.gameplay:
1. Must follow suit if possible.
2. Must try to win the trick if possible (Overtake).
3. If unable to follow suit, you must play a trump card if you have one.
4. The winner of the trick leads the next.
keyRules: If an opponent is winning the trick, must beat their card if able (subject to follow suit).
When unable to follow suit, must play a trump if you have one.
Cannot discard a seven of a non-trump suit until that suit has been led to a trick.
Trump is the suit of the dealer's last card, turned face up. Winner of each trick leads to the next.

strategy.basic: Guard your Sevens (Malillas); each is worth 5 points. Do not discard a 7 of a non-trump suit until that suit has been led. Save high trumps for when you can capture point cards.
strategy.intermediate: Signal with leads: leading a low trump can ask partner to clear trumps. Track which 7s and Aces have been played to know what is still out.
strategy.advanced: Void a weak suit early so you can trump opponents' leads and capture their Aces and Kings. Coordinate with partner without communication by consistent carding.
tips: Memory is key: track which Sevens and high cards have been played.
When an opponent is winning the trick, you must beat their card if you can (subject to follow suit).

list.name: Albur
list.description: Before first deal, one player places two cards face down; opposing team chooses one. Higher card wins 5 points and mano (right to lead to first trick). Losers deal first.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Albur adds pre-deal mano bid; engine overrides to be added when implementing this variant.

list.name: Manilla in Spain (48 cards)
list.description: Played with 48 Spanish cards (eights and nines included). The nine is highest (Manilla), not the seven. Rank 9-1-12-11-10-8-7-6-5-4-3-2. 12 cards each, 12 tricks, 72 points total. Target 40 to win. No restriction on discarding a 9 of unled suit.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses 48-card deck and different rank order; deck and trump overrides to be added when implementing.

list.name: Macau Manilla
list.description: 40 cards from 52-card pack, rank 7-A-K-J-Q-10-9-8-6-5. Jack above Queen. Points 7=5, A=4, K=3, J=2, Q=1. No bonus for turned trump. No restriction on throwing non-trump manilla. Winning team scores difference; 70 points to win game.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Macau uses different rank order and target score; overrides to be added when implementing.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't follow the 'must-overtake' rule; plays 10s into losing tricks; fails to recognize trumps.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'End-Play' optimization; perfectly tracks the remaining high cards; masters the defensive void calculation.

play_card.description: Play one card to the current trick. Must follow suit if possible. If an opponent is winning the trick, must beat their card if able (subject to follow suit). If unable to follow suit, must play a trump if you have one. Cannot discard a seven of a non-trump suit that has not yet been led.

trumpConfig.trumpSuitRanking: Seven (Malilla) high: 7, Ace, King, Horse, Jack, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2
trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Must beat opponent's winning card when possible; when unable to follow suit must play trump if able. Cannot discard a seven of a non-trump suit that has not been led.

edgeCases.text: Reneging (failing to follow suit, failing to beat opponent's winning card when able, or discarding a 7 of an unled non-trump suit) loses the whole game.

If the dealer's turned trump has point value, dealer's team scores that bonus immediately unless it would win the game; then the hand is played first and bonus applied only if neither team wins from play.
Deal irregularity (wrong number of cards, card exposed other than dealer's last): deal is void, next player deals.

engine.rankingSystem: Within each suit, from high to low: 7 (Malilla), Ace, King, Horse, Jack, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2. Trick won by highest trump, or if no trumps by highest card of suit led.
engine.deckDescription: A 40-card Spanish deck with four suits and ranks 1 through 7 plus face cards (e.g. Sota, Caballo, Rey), used in many Spanish and Latin American games.
engine.suitDescription: Suits and ranks are as defined in the deck description above; no separate suit or rank set is used for this game.

engine.dealPattern: One at a time counter-clockwise, starting with opponent to dealer's right; last card (dealer's) is turned face up to set trump suit.

scoring.description: Card points (Seven=5, Ace=4, King=3, Horse=2, Jack=1) plus one point per trick won (la negra). Total 70 points per deal. Team with more than 35 scores the difference; first to 35 cumulative wins.
scoring.winCondition: First partnership to reach 35 or more cumulative points wins. Capote: win all 10 tricks to score 35 and win the game in one deal. Zapato: reach 35 while opponents have zero.
scoring.splitRules: Team with more than 35 in the deal scores (their total minus 35); other team scores zero. Tie at 35 scores nothing.
